title: Specs Supplemental Document Schema
description: What a component needs beyond what the spec can carry, authored beside it as supplemental.yaml. The audience is whoever builds the component. Overlay-only: every entry names the schema path that cannot carry it, so anything the schema can carry belongs in the spec. What a consumer must observe is guidelines.schema.json's subject. Three scopes share this shape: one component, every component, and one foundation; entries across scopes are additive rather than overriding (DSPEC-56). This file is self-contained — its sibling documents declare their own header, verification and reference definitions rather than sharing one with it. (ADR-118)

anatomy.description: Requirements about the element tree: what parts a component has and how they nest.

props.description: Requirements about the props a component takes, and what a caller may pass.

styles.description: Requirements about the style values a component's parts carry.

slotComposition.description: Requirements about what may fill a slot, in what quantity, and in what arrangement.

events.description: Requirements about what a component emits, and when.

accessibility.description: Requirements about what assistive technology receives, and what a caller must supply for it.

behavior.description: Requirements about what a component does in response to interaction or state.

motion.description: Requirements about how a component traverses a change rather than where it ends up.

layout.description: Requirements about how a component's parts are arranged and sized relative to each other.

overrides.description: Requirements about what a caller may replace or supply in place of a component's own part.

naming.description: Requirements about why a component, prop, or part carries the name it does.

SupplementalMeta.description: Authorship and review status for the document as a whole. Every member is optional; status is the member that earns the block, because nothing else distinguishes a proposal from ratified content.

concern.description: The subject this document covers, restating what the containing directory names — a foundation concern at the foundation scope, a component name at the component scope.

status.description: Where the document sits in its review cycle.

oneOf.description: Drafted and awaiting a ratifier; its statements are not yet the system's position.
Reviewed and adopted; its statements are the system's position.
Superseded or withdrawn; kept for the record and not to be followed.

author.description: Who authored it. Duplicates git history, and is here for a reader who will not consult git.

updated.description: When it was last revised, as YYYY-MM-DD. Hand-maintained, so it can go stale.

sources.description: The generated reports this document was synthesized from, as workspace-relative paths.

Platform.description: A platform an entry is scoped to. Each value names an emission target: the two web frameworks this system emits, the two native platforms whose single sanctioned framework makes the platform name sufficient, and a group covering both web targets at once.

oneOf.description: Lit web components, emitted by webcomponents-from-specs.
Both web targets at once; expands to react and webcomponents, and may not be named beside either leaf.
Android, as Kotlin with Jetpack Compose.

SupplementalCheckedBy.description: How a requirement is checked. The checks member names what does the checking, and is required whenever this is automated.

oneOf.description: A test or lint rule decides it, with no human reading required.
A tool surfaces candidates and a human judges them.
A human decides it, with no tool involved.

SupplementalCheck.description: A reference to what checks a requirement, inside this workspace or outside it. Exactly one member is present: to names something the workspace holds, href names something it does not. Resolution of to is DSPEC-57.

to.description: What this points at inside the workspace — a test file, a lint rule, or an item within one.

href.description: What this points at outside the workspace, as an absolute URL.

Section.description: Entries for one concern the spec cannot fully carry.

SchemaGap.description: The surface that would carry a requirement, and why it cannot. Named rather than asserted — an entry that cannot name its gap belongs in the spec.

path.description: The schema pointer or workspace-relative target that would carry this. A JSON Schema pointer is resolved by a validator (DSPEC-58); a gap in the library's own data names the report instead, because a missing motion token is not a gap in styles.schema.json.

need.description: What that target cannot express, and why it cannot.

SupplementalEntry.description: One requirement the spec cannot carry.

intent.description: A testable statement of what the component must do, written to transfer directly to a test criterion. No rationale prose.

schemaGap.description: The surface that would carry this requirement, and why it does not.

platforms.description: The platforms this applies to. Absent means every platform. Because web expands to both web targets, naming it beside react or webcomponents states one thing twice and is rejected.

checks.description: What does the checking. Required when checkedBy is automated.
